newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank merger foes weigh court move.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank merger foes weigh court move.

text.p: A community activist group said Thursday it was considering a court challenge to the proposed merger of NationsBank Corp and Boatmen's Bancshares Inc.

The group Inner City Press/Community on the Move said in a statement it was considering going to court if the Federal Reserve did not do an examination of NationsBank's NationsCredit consumer finance unit.
The group has challenged many bank mergers on grounds that the resulting combinations would leave low-income neighborhoods underserved by banking.
Inner City said it had contacted 25 state regulators and that 10 had said they either had not examined NationsCredit or had conducted reviews that did not include the question fair lending pratices.
Inner City said it had gathered information showing that NationsCredit charges "predatory" interest rates of up to 20 percent "disproportionately to people of color."

Asked to comment, Cathy Bessant, senior vice president and manager of community investment at NationsBank, said NationsCredit has a diverse customer base including all races, genders and income levels.
She said the business is not heavily focused on minority, low income or elderly people.
She also said NationsCredit and NationsBank are heavily regulated, with the states subjecting NationsCredit to regulation and the bank holding company reviewed by the Federal Reserve.

Bessant said differences in charges by NationsCredit and the bank reflect the fact that NationsCredit has higher funding costs, conducts a more people-intensive business, and "the risk profile of (its) borrowers is unquestionably higher."

Bessant said Matthew Lee, executive director of the Inner City group, was engaging in "wild innuendo and wild conclusion-drawing simply to put pressure on people to respond to issues that are not accurately raised."
She added, "We've got a strong record and we are sincere and diligent in all aspects of fair lending and community investment."

Shareholders of St Louis-based Boatmen's are scheduled to vote on the $9.6 billion merger December 20. Shareholders of Charlotte, N.C.-based NationsBank are scheduled to vote on increasing the number of outstanding shares and other merger-related matters on the same day.
Bessant said NationsBank would like to see approval of the merger from the Federal Reserve in time to close the transaction in January.
Inner City, based in New York, has been joined in its protests by the New Mexico Alliance (NMA) and Mid-South Peace & Justice Center of Memphis.
NationsBank was off 1-1/4 to 94-7/8 at midday and Boatmen's was off 11/16 to 61-9/16.
